sanskrit: abhi tvendro varimataḥ purā tvāṃhūraṇebhyaḥ | hvayāmy ugraṃ cettaraṃ puruṇāmānam ekajam ||
english: I call upon Indra, who is most spacious, to protect you from the snares that have ensnared you before; I invoke the mighty one, the swift-striker, who bears many names, the sole-born.

sanskrit: yo adya senyo vadho jighāṃsan na udīrate | indrasya tatra bāhū samantaṃ pari dadhmahe ||
english: Whatever martial blow seeks to slay you today and cannot be lifted — around that we wrap the two arms of Indra on all sides.

sanskrit: pari dadhma indrasya bāhū samantaṃ trātus trāyatāṃ naḥ | deva savitaḥ soma rājan sumanasaṃ mā kṛṇutaṃ svastaye ||
english: We wrap the two arms of Indra, the protector, all around; may he protect us. O divine Savitṛ and King Soma, make us well-minded for our well-being.

sanskrit: devā aduḥ sūryo adād dyaur adāt pṛthivy adāt | sarvāḥ sarasvatīr aduḥ sacittā viṣadūṣaṇam ||
english: The gods gave it, the Sun gave it, Heaven gave it, the Earth gave it; all the Sarasvatīs, of one mind, gave the antidote to poison.

sanskrit: yad vo devā upajīkā āsiñcan dhanvany udakam | tena devaprasūtā idaṃ dūṣayatā viṣam ||
english: With the water that the gods poured into you, O grasshoppers, in the desert — with that, O god-impelled ones, corrupt this poison.

sanskrit: asurāṇām asi duhitā devānām asi svasā | divas pṛthivyā jajñiṣe sā cakarthārasaṃ viṣam ||
english: You are the daughter of the asuras, you are the sister of the gods; born of heaven and earth, you have rendered the poison powerless.

sanskrit: asthisraṃsaṃ parusraṃsam āsthitaṃ hṛdayāmayam | balāsaṃ sarvaṃ niṣ kṛdhy aṅgeṣṭhā yaś ca parvasu ||
english: The loosening of bones, the loosening of joints, what has seized the heart and made it ill — drive out entirely the balāsa-disease, that which dwells in the limbs and in the joints.

sanskrit: nir balāsaṃ balāsinaḥ kṣiṇomi puṣkaraṃ yathā | chinadmy asya bandhanaṃ mūlam urvārvo yathā ||
english: From the balāsa-afflicted man I drive out the balāsa, as one sheds a lotus; I cut its root-bond like the root of a gourd.

sanskrit: nir balāsetaḥ pra pata suparṇo vasater iva | adheṭa iva hāyano 'pa drāhy avīrahā ||
english: Fly forth from here, O balāsa, like a fine-winged bird from its nest; like a yearling colt freed from its tether, flee away — you killer of heroes.

sanskrit: ā vṛṣāyasva śvasihi vardhasva prathayasva ca | yathāṅgaṃ vardhatāṃ te śepas tena yoṣitam uj jahi ||
english: Swell up, breathe, grow, and spread out; let your phallus grow as the limb grows — with that, arouse the woman.

sanskrit: yenā kṛśaṃ medayanti yena hinvanty āturam | tenāsya brahmaṇaspate dhanur ivā tānayā pasaḥ ||
english: That by which they fatten the lean, that by which they invigorate the sick — with that, O Brahmaṇaspati, stretch his member like a bowstring on a bow.

sanskrit: āhaṃ tanomi te paso adhi jyām iva dhanvani | kramasva riśya iva rohitam anavaglāyatā tvam ||
english: I stretch your member, like the bowstring upon a bow; stride forth unflaggingly, like an antelope mounting a female rohit-deer.

sanskrit: devāḥ kapota iṣito yad icchan dūto nirṛtyā idam ājagāma | tasmā arcāma kṛṇavāma niṣkṛtiṃ śaṃ no astu dvipade catuṣpade ||
english: O gods, this pigeon that was sent — desiring something, it came here as a messenger of Nirṛti; let us worship it, let us perform an expiation for it. May there be peace for our bipeds and quadrupeds.

sanskrit: śivaḥ kapota iṣito no astv anāgā devāḥ śakuno gṛhe naḥ | agnir hi vipro juṣatāṃ havir naḥ pari hetiḥ pakṣiṇī no vṛṇaktu ||
english: May the sent pigeon be auspicious to us; O gods, may the bird in our house be blameless. May the wise Agni accept our oblation; may the winged arrow turn aside from us.

sanskrit: hetiḥ pakṣiṇī na dabhāty asmān āṣṭrī padaṃ kṛṇute agnidhāne | śaṃ no gobhya uta puruṣebhyo mā no devā iha hiṃsīt kapotaḥ ||
english: The winged arrow does not harm us; the fire-kindler makes a foothold at the fire-altar. May there be welfare for our cattle and our men; may the pigeon not injure us here, O gods.

sanskrit: iṣaṃ madantaḥ pari gāṃ nayāmaḥ saṃyopayanto duritā padāni | ṛcā kapotaṃ nudata praṇodaṃ hitvā na ūrjaṃ pra patāt patiṣṭhaḥ ||
english: Rejoicing in refreshment, let us drive the cow around, stopping up the stations of misfortune. With the verse drive off the pigeon, driving it away; may the one who dwells with us fly forth, abandoning us, to find strength elsewhere.

sanskrit: nude tvā pra ṇude tvā kapota rakṣasā saha | yato na punar āyasi tatra tvā gamayāmasi ||
english: I push you away, I drive you forth, O pigeon, along with the rakṣas; we send you to that place from which you will not come back again.

sanskrit: yathāyaṃ vāho aśvinā samaiti saṃ ca vartate | evā mām abhi te manaḥ samaitu saṃ ca vartatām ||
english: As this draught-animal, O Aśvins, comes together and moves in harmony — so let your mind come together toward me and move in harmony.

sanskrit: ahaṃ khidāmi te mano rājāśvaḥ pṛṣṭyām iva | reṣmacchinnaṃ yathā tṛṇaṃ mayi te veṣṭatāṃ manaḥ ||
english: I press your mind as a royal horse presses the spine; as grass cut by a sickle, so let your mind be wound around me.

sanskrit: āñjanasya madhughasya kuṣṭhasya naladasya ca | turo bhagasya hastābhyām anurodhanam ā bhare ||
english: Of the collyrium, of the sweet-smelling herb, of the kuṣṭha plant, and of the nalada — I bring the swift compeller of Fortune with both hands.

sanskrit: ayam ā yāty aryamā purastād viṣitastukaḥ | sa icchād agruvai patim atho jāyām ajānaye ||
english: Here comes Aryaman from the east, with loosened forelock; may he seek a husband for the unmarried girl, and also a wife for the un-fathered man.

sanskrit: aśramad iyam aryamann anyāsāṃ samanaṃ yatī | aṅgo nv asyā aryamann anyā samanam āyati ||
english: She grew weary, O Aryaman, going to the assembly of others; O Aryaman, surely now another comes to her assembly.

sanskrit: dhātā dādhāra pṛthivīṃ dhātā dyām uta sūryam | dhātāsyā agruvai patiṃ dadhātu pratikāmyam ||
english: Dhātṛ has upheld the earth; Dhātṛ has upheld the sky and the sun; may Dhātṛ bestow upon this unmarried girl a desirable husband.

sanskrit: mahyam āpo madhumad erayanta mahyaṃ sūryo abharaj jyotiṣā kam | mahyaṃ devā uta viśve tapojā mahyaṃ devaḥ savitā vyaco dhāt ||
english: The waters sent sweetness to me; the Sun brought me radiant desire; for me the gods and all the heat-born ones — for me the god Savitṛ has established expanse.

sanskrit: ahaṃ dādhāra pṛthivīm uta dyām ahaṃ sindhūn ajanaṃ sapta sākam | ahaṃ satyam anṛtaṃ yad vadāmy ahaṃ vācaṃ pari sarvām iṣiṃ ca ||
english: I have upheld the earth and the sky; I brought forth the seven rivers together; whatever truth and falsehood I speak — I encompass all speech and all desire.

sanskrit: ahaṃ vivyajmi pṛthivīm uta dyām aham ṛtūn asṛje sapta sākam | ahaṃ vācaṃ pari sarvāṃ babhūva yo agnīṣomāv ajuṣe sakhāyau ||
english: I pervade the earth and the sky; I released the seven seasons together; I have come to encompass all speech — I who have enjoyed Agni and Soma as companions.

sanskrit: anaḍudbhyo naḥ prathamaṃ dhenubhyas tvam arundhati | adhenave vayase śarma yaccha catuṣpade ||
english: For our draught-oxen first, for our milch-cows, O Arundhatī — grant shelter to the non-milking one, to the fledgling, to the four-footed.

sanskrit: śarma yacchāty oṣadhiḥ saha devair arundhatī | karat payasvantaṃ goṣṭham ayakṣmām̐ uta pūruṣān ||
english: The plant Arundhatī, together with the gods, grants shelter; may she make the cow-pen rich in milk and the men free from disease.

sanskrit: viśvarūpāṃ subhagām acchā vadāmi jīvalām | sā no rudrasyāstāṃ hetiṃ dūraṃ nayatu gobhyaḥ ||
english: I invoke the all-formed, the fortunate, the life-giving one; may she carry far away from our cattle the shaft of Rudra.

sanskrit: yamo mṛtyur aghamāro nirṛtho bhavaḥ śarvo astā nīlaśikhaṇḍī | devajanāḥ senām uttasthivāṃsas te asmākaṃ pari vṛñjantu vīrān ||
english: Yama, Death, the sin-slayer Nirṛti, Bhava, Śarva the archer, the blue-crested one — may these divine beings, who have risen up in battle-array, guard our heroes round about.

sanskrit: manasā homair harasā ghṛtena śarvāyāstra uta rājñe bhavāya | namasyebhyo nama ebhyaḥ kṛṇomy anyatrāsmad aghaviṣā nayantu ||
english: With mind, with oblations, with the fire, with ghee — to Śarva the archer and to King Bhava — I make obeisance to those worthy of obeisance; may they lead the evil poisons away from us to elsewhere.

sanskrit: trāyadhvaṃ no aghaviṣābhyo vadhād agnīṣomā marutaḥ pūtadakṣāḥ | viśve devā maruto vaiśvadevā vātāparjanyayoḥ sumatau syāma ||
english: Protect us from the evil poisons, from slaying — O Agni, Soma, and Maruts of pure might; O All-Gods, Maruts, Vaiśvadeva, may we be in the good graces of Vāta and Parjanya.

sanskrit: saṃ jānatāṃ manasā saṃ cikitvā mā yutsata manyunā daivyena | mā ghoṣa utthād bahule vinirhate meṣuḥ paptad indrasyāhany āgate ||
english: Let them know together in mind, let them be of one accord in understanding; let them not fight with divine wrath. Let no tumult arise on the great day of conflict; let the striker fall on the day of Indra's arrival.

sanskrit: saṃ vo manāṃsi saṃ vratā sam ākūtīr nayāmasi | ime ye vivratā stha tān vaḥ saṃ jñapayāmasi ||
english: We bring together your minds, your vows, your intentions; these who are of divided vow — them we cause to know together with you.

sanskrit: saṃjñapanaṃ vo manaso atho saṃ jñapanaṃ hṛdaḥ | atho bhagasya yac chrāntaṃ tena saṃ jñapayāti vaḥ ||
english: The bringing-together of your minds, and also the bringing-together of your hearts — that which is the wearied share of Fortune, with that he brings you into accord.

sanskrit: saṃ vaḥ pṛcyantāṃ tanvaḥ saṃ manāṃsi sam u tvacaḥ | saṃ vo brahmaṇaspatiḥ somaḥ saṃ jñapayāti vaḥ ||
english: Let your bodies come together, your minds together, and your skins together; Brahmaṇaspati and Soma bring you into mutual accord.

sanskrit: saṃjñānaṃ naḥ svebhyaḥ saṃjñānam araṇebhyaḥ | saṃjñānam aśvinā yuvam ihāsmāsu ni yacchatam ||
english: Accord with our own people, accord with strangers — O Aśvins, you two, bestow accord here upon us.

sanskrit: yathādityā vasavaḥ saṃbabhūvur marudbhir ugrā ahṛṇīyamānāḥ | evā triṇāmann ahṛṇīyamāna imaṃ janaṃ saṃmanasaṃ kṛṇu tvam ||
english: As the Ādityas and Vasus came together — fierce Maruts without enmity — so, O three-named one, without enmity, make this people of one mind.

sanskrit: nir amun nuda okasaḥ sapatno yaḥ pṛtanyati | nirbādhyena haviṣā- -indra enaṃ parāśarīt ||
english: Drive that rival from his dwelling — he who makes war; with the oblation that drives away, O Indra, shatter him completely.

sanskrit: ihi tisraḥ parāvata ihi pañca janām̐ ati | ihi saptāti rocanā yāvat sūryo asad divi ||
english: Go to the three distant realms, go beyond the five peoples; go to the seven luminous regions — as far as the Sun is in the sky.

sanskrit: paramāṃ tvā parāvatam indro devo ajīgamat | yathā na punar āyasi śaśvatībhyaḥ samābhyaḥ ||
english: The divine Indra has driven you to the most distant remote region, so that you will not come back for endless years.

sanskrit: pratīcīnaphalo hi tvam apāmārga babhūvitha | sarvān mac chapathām̐ adhi varīyo yāvayā tvam ||
english: For you, O apāmārga plant, have come to be one whose fruit faces backward; ward off all curses from me, warding them farther and farther away.

sanskrit: yac ca bhrātṛvyaḥ śapati yac ca jāmiḥ śapāti naḥ | brahmā yan manyutaḥ śapāt sarvaṃ tan no adhaspadam ||
english: Whatever a rival curses, whatever a kinsman curses against us, whatever a Brahmin curses out of anger — all that let be under our feet.

sanskrit: aghadviṣṭā devajūtā vīruc chapathayāvanī | udnā malam ivāvānaik sarvān mac chapathām̐ adhi ||
english: She who hates evil, who is god-impelled, the radiant one, the driver-away of curses — she has washed away all curses from me like filth with water.

sanskrit: yad enaṃ pariṣīdanti samādadhati cakṣase | saṃpreddho agnir jihvābhir ud eti hṛdayād adhi ||
english: When they sit around him, when they compose him for inspection — the kindled fire rises up with its tongues from above the heart.

sanskrit: agneḥ sāntapanasyāham āyuṣe padam ā rabhe | addhātir yasya paśyati dhūmam udyantam āsyataḥ ||
english: I take hold of the station of Agni, the mighty scorcher, for life; the one who cannot be prevented sees the smoke rising from his mouth.

sanskrit: yo asya samidhaṃ veda kṣatriyeṇa samāhitām | nābhihvāre padaṃ ni dadhāti sa mṛtyave ||
english: He who knows this kindling-wood laid together with a kṣatriya — he who does not set his foot in the crooked place, he is for death.

sanskrit: nainaṃ ghnanti paryāyiṇo na sannām̐ ava gacchati | agner yaḥ kṣatriyo vidvān nāma gṛhṇāty āyuṣe ||
english: The circling ones do not slay him; he does not sink down among the prostrate — that kṣatriya who, knowing, utters the name of Agni for long life.
